sentences.text:
Smt. G. Radha And 4 Others vs G. Sathish And Another on 6
August, 2025
 The Hon'Ble Justice B.R.Madhusudhan Rao
 MACMA.No.49 of 2022
Judgment:

entities.text: G. Radha And 4 Others vs G. Sathish And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1. This appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the MV Act, 1988)

arises out of an award passed by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - cum - XIV Additional Chief Judge (Fast Track Court), City Civil Courts, Hyderabad (for short, 'the Tribunal') in MVOP.No.
189 of 2015 dated 20.01.2021.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - cum - XIV Additional Chief Judge (Fast Track Court), City Civil Courts, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Appellants have filed claim petition for compensation under Section 166 of the MV Act, 1988 claiming an amount of Rs.30,00,000/- together with cost and interest at the rate of 18% per annum from the respondents jointly and severally.

3.1 On 25.06.2012 at about 06.00 p.m.,, G.Sadanandam was riding Hero Honda motor cycle from the house of Somavarapu Satyanarayana, MLA, Godavari Khani to his house, when he reached Labour Court at Godavari Khani, the rider of the Pulsar motor cycle bearing No.AP-15S-9596 drove the same in rash and negligent manner, suddenly took turn on right side without applying indicator or showing signs and hit the vehicle of G.Sadanandam.
As a result the G.Sadanandam received grievous BRMR, J injuries, he was shifted to Chemeda Anand Rao hospital for treatment, while undergoing treatment, he died.

3.2 The deceased was earning an amount of Rs.10,000/- per month as a driver, used to contribute his entire amount towards the maintenance of the family and was aged about 32 years as on the date of the accident.
Accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Pulsar motor cycle.

On the complaint,
police Ramagundam registered a case in Crime No. 61 of 2012 under Sections 304-A and 337 of IPC against the rider of the crime vehicle and prayed to allow the O.P.
4.
Respondent No.1 filed counter and contended that he is the owner and possessor of crime vehicle and he came to know through the petitioners that the deceased died.
5. Respondent No.2 filed counter contending that the accident occurred due to negligence of the deceased.
The driver of the Pulsar motor cycle bearing NO.AP-15S-9596 was not having valid driving licence as on the date of accident [25.06.2012].
The claim of the appellants is excessive and they are in collusion with the respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 did not inform about the accident to respondent No.2 as required under Section 134(c) of M.V.Act and respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation.
BRMR, J 6.

The Tribunal has framed the following issues:
Smt. G. Radha And 4 Others vs G. Sathish And Another on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166758158/
1 1) Whether the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the Pulsar motor cycle bearing No.AP-15S-9596?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

entities.text: Smt. G. Radha And 4 Others vs G. Sathish And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
If so, to what extent and from whom?
3) To what relief?
7.
Appellant No.1 is examined as PW1, examined PW2- B.Sathish, PW3-Somarapu Satyanarayana and got marked Exs.A1 to A8.
Respondents did not choose to adduce any evidence and got mark Ex.B1-Policy certificate.

8. The Tribunal after going through the evidence let by the parties and perusing the documents, has awarded compensation of Rs.7,95,750/- together with cost and accrued interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing the petition till the date of realization.
9. Notice to respondent No.1 is served in the appeal but he failed to appear.
10. Appellants' counsel filed memo on 13.02.2025 stating that appellant Nos.1, 4 and 5 died leaving behind appellant Nos.2 and 3 as their only legal heirs and successors.
BRMR, J 11.
Learned counsel for the appellants-petitioners submits that the award passed by the Tribunal is contrary to law, weight of evidence and probabilities of the case.

The Tribunal ought to have granted compensation as claimed by them, failed to grant interest at the rate of 9% per annum, failed to consider oral and documentary evidence produced by the appellants and has also not taken into consideration Ex.A7-salary certificate.
The Tribunal ought to have taken the salary of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month but instead thereof has taken only Rs.4,500/- per month and prayed to enhance the compensation.
In support of his contention has relied on the decisions in the case of M.H.Uma Maheshwari and Others.
Vs. United India Insurance Co.Ltd & another. 1 and (ii) New India Assurance Co.Ltd., vs. Srikantha and others 2

entities.text: New India Assurance Co.Ltd., vs. Srikantha and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that order and decree passed by the Tribunal is reasonable and needs no interference of the Court, on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 41 years 3 months 15 days and the wages of the deceased to be considered as Rs.6,000/- per month and prayed to pass appropriate orders.

Learned counsel for the appellant has filed calculation memo showing the income of the deceased as Rs.10,000/- per month and learned counsel for respondent No.2 filed calculation memo showing the income of the deceased as Rs.6,000/- per month.
Smt. G. Radha And 4 Others vs G. Sathish And Another on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166758158/
2 14.

entities.text: G. Radha And 4 Others vs G. Sathish And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties, perused the record.
15. Now the point for consideration is: whether the appellants are entitled for enhancement of compensation, if so, to what amount?
16. The Tribunal has fixed the income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/- per month.

PW1 deposed that her husband G.Sadanandam worked as a driver with Somavarapu Satyanarayana MLA,
Godavarikani, and he used to earn Rs.10,000/- per month, he is the sole earner of the family and he used to contribute his entire income towards maintenance of the family, due to sudden death of G.Sadanandam herself and other family members have suffered financially.
17. PW3 is the MLA of Ramagundam, his evidence is that deceased G.Sadanandam was working under him as a driver since five years and his salary is Rs.10,000/- per month.

In his cross- examination he stated that he is an income tax assesse, he used to show all his expenditure incurred in his Income Tax Returns, he used to mention in his IT returns under the head of salaries along BRMR, J with other employees but could not file any documents as during the transit the records were misplaced and he is not in a position to produce the same.
18.1 Since the accident occurred on 25.06.2012, the deceased is a driver by profession, if an amount of Rs.8,000/- is fixed towards salary will meet the ends of justice.
Learned counsel for respondent No.2 has not disputed the multiplier adopted by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has awarded consortium to appellant No.1/petitioner No.1 only to an amount of Rs.44,000/- but lost sight of the other petitioners who were entitled for parental consortium as per the judgment of the Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Vs. Pranay Sethi 3.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Vs. Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18.2 It is to be noted that during the pendency of the appeal appellant Nos.1, 4 and 5 died leaving behind appellant Nos.2 and 3 as the only legalheirs and successors.
The right to claim consortium is generally considered as a personal right of the individual, who has suffered the loss.
It is not a right that can be inherited or passed on to their legal representatives as such appellant Nos.2 and 3 are only entitled for consortium.
19. There is no dispute with regard to deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased G.Sadanandam.

The (2017) 16 SCC 680 BRMR, J decision cited by the appellants' counsel in M.H.Uma Maheshwari's case1 do not assist them in any manner in view of the fact that the respondent No.2 has not disputed the multiplier applied by the Tribunal i.e., '14' as the deceased G.Sadanandam was in the age group of 41-45.

The Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of filing the petition till the date of realization which is on the lower side and the appellants are entitled for interest at the rate of 9% per annum as per the decision of the Supreme Court in Anjali and Others vs. Lokendra Rathod and others 4.
20.

entities.text: Anjali and Others vs. Lokendra Rathod and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 shall follow the guidelines while dealing with the aspect of determination of correctness or otherwise of the TDS (Tax Deduction at Source) in case of motor accident claims as per the decision in New India Assurance Company Limited2.

sentences.text:
. In the result, MACMA.No.49 of 2022 is partly allowed and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced as under:
Smt. G. Radha And 4 Others vs G. Sathish And Another on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166758158/
4 a) The impugned award dated 20.01.2021, passed in MVOP.No. 189 of 2015, stands modified.
b) The compensation awarded by the Tribunal i.e., Rs.7,95,750/- is enhanced to Rs.13,81,000/- together with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of filing the petition till payment.
c) Appellants-petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are entitled to Rs.6,90,500/- each and they are permitted to withdraw the entire amount with costs and interest thereon without furnishing security.
